text:
julia: Heads up, autodrain kicked for node gpu-cc-17 in us-west-2c — ECC correctable spiked + repeated Xid 79. infra-bot scheduled a staggered cordon/drain.

infra-bot: Detected gpu_ecc_correctable_total > 200 over 5m and nvml_xid_errors > 3. Initiating autodrain-splay policy (splay_window=10m, max_parallel=1). Cordon -> live drain -> post-drain health check.

omar: Thanks. Can someone confirm why splay_window is 10m? we don't want capacity cliffs during peak.

sasha: We added splay to avoid mass evictions when a noisy telemetry storm hits multiple nodes at once. Default 10m is conservative; we've used 5m in pre-prod. For prod inference pools I'd keep 10m + max_parallel=1.

matt: Ops question: when the node is cordoned first, do we drain pods immediately or wait for graceful window? what about latency-sensitive inference pods?

sasha: We perform graceful eviction with a 2m drain timeout for LATENCY_SENSITIVE taint exception groups. For those, we try soft-migrate by telling the scheduler to prefer other nodes, then if still running after 2m we hard-evict.

anita: For Slurm batches on GPU nodes we mark node as DRAIN with reason and set a delay so running jobs can finish short ones; long jobs get requeued. Example: `scontrol update NodeName=gpu-cc-17 State=DRAIN Reason="ecc-xid-autodrain"`

omar: How do we detect the Xid spike source? hardware vs driver? we don't want to replace for transient driver flakiness.

julia: The runbook checks three signals before replacement: 1) persistent ECC correctable growth over 3 windows, 2) Xid class >= 79 repeated, 3) nvml GPU reset count > 1 in 30m. If only Xid once, we only cordon+reboot and monitor.

infra-bot: Runbook step executed: cordon gpu-cc-17, drain started at 1768001247, grace_period=120s, splay_window_remaining=08m53s.

matt: Can we see the Prometheus rule used for the alert? need to share with paging config.

sasha: Here's the alert we use (simplified):

```
- alert: GPU_ECC_And_XID_Anomaly
  expr: (
    increase(dcgm_gpu_ecc_correctable_total[5m]) > 100
    and increase(nvml_xid_errors_total[5m]) > 2
  )
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "GPU ECC/XID anomaly on {{ $labels.instance }}"
```

anita: When a node is drained we also auto-apply `gpu_quarantine=true` label so placement policies avoid it post-reboot until healthcheck passes.

omar: How do we avoid draining multiple nodes in the same AZ? We had an incident where 3/4 GPUs in a rack went out because of simultaneous drains.

sasha: Our controller reads `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` and enforces `max_parallel_per_zone=1`. It also prefers to pick nodes across zones if available. That's the splay.

julia: Also we have a capacity-safety check: if free_gpu_fraction < 0.12 in pool, autodrain will only cordon and escalate to oncall human for manual approval.

matt: For Dedicated pools that run production inference, we sometimes prefer to fallback to a cheaper CPU-backed path rather than draining nodes during spike windows. Is that integrated?

sasha: Yes — routing policy will shift requests to compatible model variants in the same region for up to 5m. We annotate nodes with `pool=dedicated-inference` and routing rules read that.

infra-bot: Health-check post-drain: nvml_gpu_reset_count=0, dcgm_ecc_stable=true, nvml_xid_errors=0 for 15m -> uncordon. Current node state: rebooting (automation triggered).

omar: Quick ops commands for folks:
```
# Kubernetes cordon and drain
kubectl cordon gpu-cc-17
kubectl drain gpu-cc-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120 --force
# Slurm drain
scontrol update NodeName=gpu-cc-17 State=DRAIN Reason="ecc-xid-autodrain"
```

anita: Note: for preemptible/gpu-burst nodes we also apply taint `redwood.io/autodrain=temporary:NoSchedule` so DaemonSets unaffected.

julia: Follow-up tasks: 1) add a short audit event to console when autodrain starts (so customers can see transient capacity change) 2) add a dashboard panel showing splay windows active across zones 3) docs for SRE on how to override max_parallel in emergency. I'll take 1+3.

sasha: I'll add the alert snippet to the alerting repo and open a PR to support `max_parallel_per_zone` config.

matt: I'll touch base with model infra to ensure model fallbacks are enabled for dedicated inference pools during drains.

infra-bot: Autodrain summary: 1 node affected, splay enforced, no paging to oncall (capacity ok). Marking thread resolved but leaving logs in #eng-infra. :white_check_mark:

julia: thanks — closing after post-reboot healthcheck passes. :thumbsup:
